title: A stored `expression` field added to an object that already has rows is never backfilled: existing rows stay NULL until each is next written
body:
Found by the hotclm app (objectstack-ai/hotclm#31, PR #201) on `@objectstack/*` 18.3.0.

**What happens.** hotclm adds a stored expression field to `clm_contract`: `review_sla_days_offset = 0 - record.contract_type.review_sla_days`. Booting that change over a database created before it (`pnpm demo:zh` on the previous main) left the column NULL on 121 of 121 rows. A later seed pass rewrote only 41 of 120 rows, leaving 79 NULL. A fresh database is fine (0 NULL), because every insert computes the value.

**Why it matters.** The value is computed only on the write path, so on an upgraded database the field is silently wrong until each row is touched. In hotclm the analytics `$now` anchor (`{ $now: true, addDays: { $field: 'review_sla_days_offset' } }`, #25808) reads a NULL offset as 0 days, so every started review counts as over SLA: the dashboard over-counts with no error.

**Seam.** `spec: Field.expression` (stored, `field.zod.ts`) → runtime: objectql `computeStoredExpressions` (write path only). `os migrate` has a summary-nulls step for roll-ups but nothing that recomputes a stored expression for existing rows.

**Expected.** Adding (or changing) a stored expression either backfills existing rows at boot / schema sync, or `os migrate` offers a recompute step and the boot log says the column needs it, the same honest-disclosure shape as the roll-up backfill.

Dedupe: no issue matches "stored expression backfill", "expression field NULL existing rows" or "recompute stored expression"; #27193 is a currency-specific recompute.
